### Generate chart data from session logs on every sync

[`3d51cd932fb8`](https://github.com/pilifs/in-the-loop/commit/3d51cd932fb8e02597363b71379ce64da239d648) · [log `7e414e54d4f3`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/24d088fa-8a2f-419c-9283-2557487b7d9f/7e414e54d4f3ec4b1b6e1c8f73ca2c4d8ec26c683d91f0513ae4767830199488.jsonl.gz)

Add llm-dlc/tools/metrics.py, which turns each redacted log into llm-dlc/traces/&lt;session-id>/metrics.json: every prompt, model call, tool call, compaction, pause and large cache write as tables, with list-price costs from the new hand-written llm-dlc/pricing.json. llm-dlc/traces/metrics.json adds them up over all sessions, by model, effort, tool, day, session and commit. This is the data layer for charts like the ones in the reading-the-trace blog post, which came from one-off scripts run on one log with hand-typed prices, labels and annotations.

Beyond what those scripts did: work is attributed to commits by the line count of each commit's log; cache writes get a derived cause and every other factor present, which replaces the hand-written notes; time uses interval unions, because parallel tool calls overlap; prompts are told apart from commands and tool results; and Claude Code's own cost-state record is kept beside the computed cost, because compaction and Haiku side calls are missing from logs.

sync.py writes the files on every commit and push. check rebuilds each one from its log, fails if it differs or if its token totals differ from the manifest, scans it for leaks, and warns about models with no price. Verified on the post's log prefix: 327 calls, 364 tool calls, 25 prompts, every token total and the $39.35 / $284.85 costs match its session.json exactly. Computed costs reproduce cost-state to the cent per model. Usage sums to the totals across prompts, windows and commits on all sessions. test_metrics.py has 21 tests on made-up sessions.

### Let a person mark findings as false positives

[`4e47aee07118`](https://github.com/pilifs/in-the-loop/commit/4e47aee071187981445c0fdd64fb21298c3f0e2f) · [log `aea563c89ba5`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/24d088fa-8a2f-419c-9283-2557487b7d9f/aea563c89ba52dcda61b1df8d91037858f74902f41987825ed54232596cd7e0c.jsonl.gz)

Warnings came back with every log snapshot, because the only way to quiet one was to accept a whole log by hash, and each new snapshot has a new hash. sync.py now keeps a published list of reviewed findings. An entry covers one kind and one exact value, stored as a hash with the reason, who decided and when, so it lasts across snapshots while a different value of that kind is still raised. check, scan, push and the upload guard all honour it, for errors as well as warnings, and check notes how many findings it left out. Local secrets and account identifiers can never be waived.

Recording a finding needs a person: the accept command shows the real value, asks for a typed confirmation, and refuses a shell with no terminal or one Claude Code started. The project settings deny agents direct edits, and CLAUDE.md tells them to ask. These guard against accidents, not determined evasion; the published history of the list is the record. Listing open findings stays open, masked.

The list starts with the four findings the maintainer authorized in chat: the Authorization: Bearer sentence from the API skill documentation, the made-up home path from the metrics tests, and two Cloudflare addresses in dig output for the CDN domain. Each was located with masked output first. Verified with 10 new tests in test_review.py, by accept being refused from this agent's shell, and by review reporting no open findings.

## What gets generated
| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `llm-dlc/traces/<session-id>/metrics.json` | Tables for prompts, model calls, tool calls, commits, context windows, compactions, pauses and cache events, plus totals |
| `llm-dlc/traces/metrics.json` | All sessions added up by model, effort, tool, Bash program, cache cause, day, session and commit; 27 KB, so a page can load it alone |
| `llm-dlc/pricing.json` | Hand-maintained list prices, which replace the prices hard-coded in `charts.py` |

- **Code and docs:** the logic is in `llm-dlc/tools/metrics.py`, and the schema is documented under *Metrics* in `specification.md`.
- **New compared with the blog scripts:**
  - It covers every session, not just one.
  - It gives cost per commit.
  - It works out cache-spike causes automatically instead of using hand-written notes.
  - It separates typed prompts from slash commands: one session has 26 typed prompts, but its manifest counts 50 turns.
- **Size:** the generated files add about 610 KB to the repo. Rows are one per line, so later commits should only add new rows to the diffs.
